headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns
summary: Top Republican lawmakers have requested Jensen Huang appear for a closed-door briefing on November 18, following reports of him being targeted by a Chinese spy operation regarding sensitive US tech.
details: Top Republican lawmakers have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to appear before Congress. The summons comes after reports that US intelligence officials believe Huang has been targeted by a Chinese spying operation.

The chairs of the House committees on China, foreign affairs, and intelligence wrote to Huang this week. They requested his appearance at a joint closed-door briefing for their committees on November 18.

Lawmakers stated that recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive US technology and information. They emphasized the importance of determining the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk.

The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials believe Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation. Concerns center on Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud company that has purchased billions of dollars of Nvidia chips.

Nvidia has rejected these claims, stating that meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job. The company added that regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information, not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets or national security-relevant data.

Lawmakers want Huang to discuss Nvidia's security protocols to protect against foreign adversary espionage. Nvidia responded that its chief executive has an "outstanding security team" that travels with him.

The New York Times noted that Huang had not received a "defensive briefing," which the intelligence community usually provides to potential espionage targets. Nvidia expressed confidence that the US government would have informed them if a person was a threat.

Megaspeed, founded in 2023, has previously been scrutinized by the US for potential chip smuggling, though no charges followed. Nvidia conducted its own on-site inspections at Megaspeed, finding no evidence of chips being diverted to China.

Nvidia's supply chain faces increasing scrutiny due to US export controls leading to increased chip smuggling. Earlier this year, Wally Liaw, a co-founder of Supermicro, was arrested and charged with smuggling Nvidia chips into China, a charge he denies.

headline_marked: [[Amazon launches text-to-shop with Alexa]] for select US customers, rolling out broadly soon
headline: Amazon launches text-to-shop with Alexa for select US customers, rolling out broadly soon
summary: Customers can now text Alexa to search for items, add to cart, purchase, and even reorder by sharing photos, starting with select US users.
details: Amazon is launching a new feature that allows customers to chat with its Alexa AI agent via text messages for shopping assistance. This enables natural language queries to search for items, add them to a cart, and complete purchases directly through text.

The text agent builds on recent Alexa shopping upgrades, supporting tasks like managing lists, tracking prices, comparing products, and checking order statuses. Users can also share a picture of an item to search for similar listings on Amazon.
Over time, Alexa will learn user preferences and suggest items accordingly. This move comes after Amazon previously blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site.
The feature is initially rolling out to select U.S. customers who will receive a text invitation to enable it. Those without an invitation can sign up for a waitlist.

Amazon plans a broader rollout in the coming weeks, just before the holiday shopping season. This initiative highlights the growing trend of platforms developing their own AI agents for consumer interaction, mirroring similar efforts by companies like DoorDash.
